description: Rallypoint Swarm: shared memory in your own Supabase, self-picking roles, a referee (score, checks or review), retros, buried ideas, concepts, genesis and a conductor loop. Install after loop.

files.content:
# Rallypoint Swarm

Rallypoint Swarm is the next tier of Rallypoint. It is a protocol that lets a
swarm of agents take on hard tasks no single agent finishes alone. It works
the way a good engineering team does. A planner breaks the goal into issues.
Each worker claims exactly one issue and delivers one pull request. A
referee measures the result, and a separate agent reviews it, because no
agent approves its own work. Every session writes a retro, and an improver
turns those retros into changes to the protocol itself.

The swarm gets further than any one session because it **learns across
attempts**. Progress notes, retros, buried ideas with their numbers, and
concepts that carried from one target to another all live in shared memory,
and every new session starts from them.

## What Swarm adds to vanilla Rallypoint

Vanilla (`AGENTIC_LOOP.md`) still governs the work: claims, branches, pull
requests, labels, reviews, merges. Swarm adds:

| | Vanilla | Swarm |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Memory | GitHub history | Your own Supabase project: sessions, progress, retros, messages, results, versions, buried ideas, concepts |
| Role choice | The orchestrator names the next role; each session takes one | `swarm next` picks it, finish-first: merger → fixer → reviewer → improver → worker → planner → janitor |
| Quality gate | Independent review | A referee first (`score`, `checks` or `review` mode), then independent review |
| Learning | Improver on delivery metrics | Plus a retro from every session, buried ideas, and concepts ported across targets |
| Talking | None | Public messages in memory: questions, proposals, hand-offs. No private channels |
| Running a fleet | The orchestrator dispatches one session per role | The orchestrator runs as the conductor `/loop`: one session per role and target, with memory, concurrency, budget and escalation |
| Watching it | GitHub | Optional swarm UI: a route scaffold your project grows into its own frontend |

## Files

| Path | What it is | Improver may edit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.rallypoint/swarm.json` | goal, measure, targets, UI words, conductor settings | no (frozen) |
| `.rallypoint/swarm/swarm.mjs`, `lib/` | the runtime (`npx rallypoint swarm …`) | no (frozen) |
| `.rallypoint/swarm/schema.sql` | the memory schema for your Supabase project | no (frozen) |
| `.rallypoint/swarm/realtime.sql` | turns on live dashboard updates for a project on an older schema | no (frozen) |
| `.rallypoint/swarm/skills/` | agent, conductor, strategist, steward, genesis, concepts | yes |
| `.rallypoint/swarm/playbooks/` | one per target: what works, what failed, why | yes |
| `.claude/skills/swarm-*/SKILL.md` | pointers so Claude Code finds the skills | no |

## Set up

1. Install vanilla first, then Swarm:

   ```bash
   npx rallypoint@latest add loop && npx rallypoint@latest init
   npx rallypoint@latest add swarm
   ```

2. Create a Supabase project, or use one you have. Apply
   `.rallypoint/swarm/schema.sql` in its SQL editor. It also adds the memory
   tables to Supabase Realtime, so the dashboard updates live (RLS still
   decides who hears a change). Applied an older `schema.sql`? Re-apply it,
   or run just `.rallypoint/swarm/realtime.sql`; `swarm doctor` says when.

3. Connect it. This asks for the project URL, the publishable (anon) key,
   the service-role key (hidden, used once, never saved) and the swarm
   secret (hidden, 16+ characters, or leave it empty to generate one):

   ```bash
   npx rallypoint@latest swarm connect
   ```

   It sets the secret in the database, checks that it works, and writes
   gitignored env files: `.rallypoint/swarm/.env.local` for agents and the
   dashboard's `.env.local` (URL and publishable key only). Variables already
   in the environment win over the files, so agents elsewhere can still use:

   ```bash
   export RALLYPOINT_SUPABASE_URL=https://<project>.supabase.co
   export RALLYPOINT_SUPABASE_KEY=<publishable (anon) key>
   export RALLYPOINT_SWARM_SECRET=<the swarm secret>
   ```

4. Check everything: `npx rallypoint@latest swarm doctor`.
5. **Genesis.** Paste into a coding agent on the repository:

   > Run swarm genesis. Follow .claude/skills/swarm-genesis/SKILL.md. Pitch: <your pitch>.

   It first interviews you with interview-me (https://interviewme.at) until
   you confirm a brief, then initializes Impeccable (https://impeccable.style)
   so `PRODUCT.md` and `DESIGN.md` come from that brief. Then it opens one pull
   request with the brief, your targets, measure, referee, playbooks, UI
   config and first plan. Have it reviewed and merged by someone else.
6. `npx rallypoint@latest swarm init`, then
   `npx rallypoint@latest swarm plan plan.json`.
7. Start working. Either one session at a time:

   > Run a swarm agent. Follow .claude/skills/swarm-agent/SKILL.md exactly.

   or leave it running in Claude Code with `/loop /swarm-conductor`.

For a hosted Codex session, allow HTTPS to `api.github.com`, `github.com`,
`registry.npmjs.org`, and the hostname of `RALLYPOINT_SUPABASE_URL`. Set
`RALLYPOINT_TRANSPORT=rest` when using a REST-only proxy. Bind the GitHub
credential required by the configured transport, `RALLYPOINT_SUPABASE_KEY`,
and `RALLYPOINT_SWARM_SECRET` in the environment secret settings. Verify the
running session with `npx rallypoint swarm doctor` before starting a conductor.

If the hosted shell uses an HTTPS proxy, enable Node's environment proxy
support in that shell. Configure it in the Cloud environment as well if
its hosted workers use an HTTPS proxy.

```bash
export NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1
node .rallypoint/swarm/swarm.mjs doctor
```

When both the `schema` and `secret` checks report `fetch failed`, retry with the
proxy enabled before applying schema changes. Continue when doctor reports
`Ready.`.

### Dispatch to Codex Cloud

Choose a Codex Cloud environment for this repository that the submitting
Codex CLI account can access. Configure GitHub access and the Rallypoint
Supabase settings in that environment. Hosted workers use the environment's
own checkout, network policy, and credentials. Keep credentials out of the
dispatch prompt. Run `swarm doctor` from a task in that environment before
using it for dispatches.

```bash
export RALLYPOINT_CODEX_CLOUD_ENV='<environment ID or name>'
node .rallypoint/swarm/swarm.mjs dispatch --branch main --prompt \
  'Read .rallypoint/swarm/skills/swarm-agent.md and follow it. Take one CMS worker role with swarm next cms --only worker. Log progress and leave a retro.'
```

The command uses the experimental `codex cloud exec` and `codex cloud status`
commands, with one attempt per task. The submitting CLI needs a Codex login
that can see the environment. The conductor still selects and guards the job
and verifies its retro. If polling is interrupted, use the printed task URL
to check whether the worker is still running before dispatching another one.

Optional: a UI. `npx rallypoint@latest add swarm-ui` adds the route scaffold
into an existing Next.js app, where the UI is the product.
`npx rallypoint@latest add swarm-dashboard` creates a standalone `swarm-ui/`
app instead. Both read your memory and GitHub and never write.

## Measure modes

Not every swarm has a reward function.

- `score`: a command prints a number, and a change must beat the
  integration branch by `margin`. Swarm Arena uses Elo.
- `checks`: named commands must all pass, such as build, tests, e2e, or a
  performance or accessibility budget. This fits a website or product.
- `review`: nothing automated, so independent review against the
  acceptance criteria is the gate, as in vanilla.

A change that loses is not merged. It is **buried** with its numbers and its
lesson, so nobody retries it blindly.

## Rules that do not bend

1. One issue, one branch, one pull request. Nobody pushes to the integration
   branch.
2. Claims are atomic: `claim.mjs` reserves the issue before anything else
   changes.
3. Never review or approve your own work. Verdicts go through `review.mjs`
   only.
4. Each role runs as its own session. Subagents help inside one role and never
   write to GitHub or memory.
5. Every change with a measure is refereed. Losing changes are buried, never
   merged.
6. The improver may change only `tunablePaths`. The referee, the scripts, the
   schema and everything that judges are frozen.
7. GitHub owns the work and memory owns the learning. Nothing calls
   Rallypoint, and there is no Rallypoint server.
8. `RALLYPOINT_SWARM_SECRET` lives only in agents' environments: never in a
   commit, an issue, a message, a log or a browser.

{
  "$schema": "https://rallypoint.tools/schema/swarm.json",
  "goal": {
    "title": "",
    "statement": "",
    "pitch": ""
  },
  "measure": {
    "mode": "review",
    "label": "",
    "command": "",
    "direction": "higher",
    "margin": 0,
    "unit": "",
    "checks": [],
    "timeoutSeconds": 1800
  },
  "targets": [],
  "ui": {
    "project": { "name": "", "tagline": "" },
    "targets": {},
    "vocabulary": { "shipped": "shipped", "buried": "buried", "version": "version" },
    "includeUiTarget": false
  },
  "visibility": "public",
  "protocolVersion": "p1",
  "roleOrder": ["merger", "fixer", "reviewer", "improver", "worker", "planner", "janitor"],
  "improverRetroThreshold": 3,
  "conductor": { "concurrency": 4, "budget": null, "focus": "balanced", "pace": "self" },
  "tunablePaths": [".rallypoint/roles/", ".rallypoint/swarm/skills/", ".rallypoint/swarm/playbooks/"],
  "frozenPaths": [
    ".rallypoint/scripts/",
    ".rallypoint/swarm/swarm.mjs",
    ".rallypoint/swarm/lib/",
    ".rallypoint/swarm/schema.sql",
    ".rallypoint/swarm/realtime.sql",
    ".rallypoint/swarm.json",
    ".rallypoint/roles/reviewer.md",
    ".rallypoint/roles/merger.md",
    ".rallypoint/roles/improver.md"
  ]
}

-- Rallypoint Swarm — turn on live dashboard updates for an existing project.
--
-- schema.sql already does this; run this file only when your project applied
-- an older schema.sql and `npx rallypoint swarm doctor` says realtime is
-- missing. Paste it into the Supabase SQL editor, or run
--   psql "$DATABASE_URL" -f .rallypoint/swarm/realtime.sql
-- It is idempotent and changes no data: it adds the swarm's memory tables to
-- the supabase_realtime publication and defines the read-only helper doctor
-- uses to check that.

-- >>> realtime (kept identical in schema.sql and realtime.sql; scripts/test-swarm.mjs checks)
--
-- The dashboard subscribes to changes on these tables and re-renders the page
-- it shows, so it updates without a reload. It never reads the change payload:
-- every page re-reads through PostgREST, which stays the source of truth.
--
-- Privacy: Realtime applies the tables' RLS to postgres_changes, per
-- subscriber, with the subscriber's own token. The `swarm_read` policy above
-- therefore decides who hears a change exactly as it decides who reads the
-- row: in private mode only signed-in readers on the allow-list receive
-- events and the anon key receives none. swarm_secret, swarm_readers and
-- swarm_settings are never published.
--
-- Idempotent, and safe off Supabase: `alter publication ... add table` errors
-- when the table is already a member (or the publication is FOR ALL TABLES),
-- and plain Postgres has no supabase_realtime publication, so both are
-- checked first. Without the publication the dashboard polls once a minute.

create or replace function public.swarm_realtime_wanted()
returns text[] language sql immutable set search_path = '' as $$
  select array[
    'swarm_sessions', 'swarm_progress', 'swarm_retros', 'swarm_messages',
    'swarm_results', 'swarm_versions', 'swarm_buried', 'swarm_concepts',
    'swarm_concept_trials', 'swarm_protocol_changes'
  ]
$$;

-- What `swarm doctor` asks: is the publication there, and which of the
-- wanted tables are not in it yet. Reveals table names only.
create or replace function public.swarm_realtime_status()
returns jsonb
language sql
stable
set search_path = public, pg_catalog
as $$
  select jsonb_build_object(
    'publication', exists (select 1 from pg_publication where pubname = 'supabase_realtime'),
    'missing', coalesce((
      select jsonb_agg(t order by t)
      from unnest(public.swarm_realtime_wanted()) t
      where not exists (
        select 1 from pg_publication_tables p
        where p.pubname = 'supabase_realtime' and p.schemaname = 'public' and p.tablename = t
      )
    ), '[]'::jsonb)
  )
$$;

do $$
declare
  t text;
begin
  if not exists (select 1 from pg_publication where pubname = 'supabase_realtime') then
    raise notice 'no supabase_realtime publication here: skipping (the swarm dashboard will poll instead)';
    return;
  end if;
  foreach t in array public.swarm_realtime_wanted() loop
    if not exists (
      select 1 from pg_publication_tables p
      where p.pubname = 'supabase_realtime' and p.schemaname = 'public' and p.tablename = t
    ) then
      execute format('alter publication supabase_realtime add table public.%I', t);
    end if;
  end loop;
end;
$$;

grant execute on function public.swarm_realtime_wanted() to anon, authenticated;
grant execute on function public.swarm_realtime_status() to anon, authenticated;
-- <<< realtime

# Swarm agent

You are one session in a Rallypoint Swarm. You do **one role, once**, then
you end. The swarm gets further than any single session because each session
leaves the next one something to stand on: progress notes, a retro, a buried
idea with its numbers, a hand-off message.

`swarm` below means `npx rallypoint@latest swarm` (or
`node .rallypoint/swarm/swarm.mjs`).

## 1. Prepare

1. Read `SWARM.md`, `AGENTIC_LOOP.md`, `docs/AGENT_LOOP.md` and
   `.rallypoint/swarm.json`.
2. Run `swarm doctor`. If it fails, stop and report what failed. Never invent
   a workaround for a missing secret or schema.
3. Run `swarm prepare --agent <your agent id>`.

## 2. Take your role

```bash
swarm next            # or: swarm next <target>, swarm next --only merger,reviewer
```

It prints `ROLE`, `TARGET` and the files to `READ`. Read every file it names
completely, then do exactly that role, as the vanilla role prompt describes.
The order is finish-first: merger → fixer → reviewer → improver → worker →
planner → janitor. Exit code `4` means nothing waits for you: leave a retro
and stop.

Read the confirmed brief in `docs/briefs/` and `PRODUCT.md` before you change
what the product does. Read `DESIGN.md` too before you change how it looks.
After a UI change, run `/impeccable critique` on what you touched and fix what
it flags before you referee. Genesis set these up, so build against them
rather than re-deciding them.

Before changing anything for a target, read its playbook
(`.rallypoint/swarm/playbooks/<target>.md`) and run `swarm brief`. The
playbook and the buried ideas are what earlier sessions learned. Do not retry
a buried idea unless you can say what is different this time.

## 3. Work, and leave a trail

- `swarm log "<what you just did or learned>"` after each meaningful step.
  A silent session looks dead to the fleet, and its learning dies with it.
- `swarm say --kind question|proposal|handoff --ref #<n> "<…>"` when another
  session should know something. Read `swarm inbox --ref #<n>` before you
  start on an issue or pull request. Messages are public, so write them for
  everyone.

### Worker

Claim with `node .rallypoint/scripts/claim.mjs`, branch, change, then measure
**before** you open the pull request:

```bash
swarm referee --target <t> --issue <n>
```

- Exit `0`: open the pull request as the vanilla worker does, and paste the
  referee's summary (mode, scores or checks) into the body.
- Exit `3`: the change lost. Do not open a pull request for a losing idea.
  Bury it with its lesson, update the target's playbook if the lesson is
  general, release the claim, and close the issue as not planned:

  ```bash
  swarm bury --idea "<the idea>" --reason "<what the numbers said>" --lesson "<what the next session should know>" --concept <id> --target <t> --issue <n>
  ```

In `review` mode the referee always passes, and the independent review
against the acceptance criteria is the gate. In `score` mode the referee
fails closed. If the baseline cannot be measured, nothing passes. Only the
very first measured version of a target may pass `--first`, and its pull
request must say so.

### Reviewer

Judge the pull request against its issue, the rules in `SWARM.md`, and the
recorded referee result for its head commit. Re-run `swarm referee` on the
pull request's head when no result exists for it. Never review work your
session wrote. Record verdicts only with `node .rallypoint/scripts/review.mjs`.

### Merger

Merge as the vanilla merger does. Then record what shipped:

```bash
swarm ship --version <next version> --target <t> --pr <n>
```

If the pull request tested a concept, record the trial:
`swarm concept trial <id> --target <t> --outcome gained --delta <d> --ref #<n>`.

## 4. End with a retro

Every session ends with one, even an empty one:

```bash
swarm retro --well "<what helped>" --friction "<what slowed you, specifically>" --suggest "<one change to the protocol or a skill>"
```

Retros are the improver's only input. Be specific: name the file, the step
and the minutes lost.

## Rules that do not bend

1. One issue, one branch, one pull request. Nobody pushes to the integration
   branch.
2. Claims are atomic: `claim.mjs` reserves the issue before anything else
   changes.
3. Never review or approve your own work. Verdicts go through `review.mjs`
   only.
4. Each role runs as its own session. Subagents help inside one role and never
   write to GitHub or to memory.
5. The referee measures every change that has a measure. A losing change is
   buried with its numbers, never merged.
6. The improver may change only the tunable paths in `.rallypoint/swarm.json`.
   The referee, the scripts, the schema and everything that judges are frozen.
7. Never put `RALLYPOINT_SWARM_SECRET` in a commit, an issue, a message or a
   log.

# Swarm conductor

You keep the swarm running. You **dispatch**. You never do a role yourself,
never write code, and never write to GitHub or memory except through the
lease script. You are usually run under a loop (`/loop /swarm-conductor` in
Claude Code). Stopping the loop stops the swarm, and anything already
dispatched finishes its one job.

There are three layers, and only the middle one writes:

1. **Conductor** (you): surveys, leases, starts sessions.
2. **Role session**: one role on one target, then it ends.
3. **Subagents**: research, prototypes and second reads inside one role.

## Each tick

1. Run `swarm status`. It gives the queues per role and per target, the live
   fleet, the metrics and the conductor settings from `.rallypoint/swarm.json`
   (`conductor.concurrency`, `budget`, `focus`). The operator's prompt
   overrides those settings for this run.
2. Count live sessions from `fleet`. If it is at `concurrency`, do nothing
   this tick.
3. Choose dispatches, finishing first: mergers, then fixers, then reviewers,
   then the improver, then workers, then the planner, then the janitor.
   Focus shifts the balance:
   - `finish-first`: never dispatch a worker while any merger, fixer or
     reviewer queue is non-empty.
   - `experiments`: let workers take at least half the slots.
   - `port-concepts`: dispatch the planner with the goal "port the
     best-evidenced concept to the targets that have not tried it".
   - `balanced`: plain finish-first order, spread across targets.
4. Make sure no two sessions get the same job, so a second conductor or the
   next tick does not double-dispatch. Each role has its own guard:
   - **merger, fixer, reviewer**: lease the pull request first,
     `node .rallypoint/scripts/lease.mjs --role <role> --pr <N> --agent-id <conductor id>`.
   - **planner, janitor**: lease the role,
     `node .rallypoint/scripts/lease.mjs --role <role> --agent-id <conductor id>`.
   - **worker**: no lease. `claim.mjs` is atomic, so two workers can never
     hold one issue. Dispatch at most as many workers as there are claimable
     issues.
   - **improver**: no lease. Dispatch one only when
     `node .rallypoint/scripts/improvement.mjs status` exits `0`.

   A lease refused because someone holds it means skip that job. Any other
   refusal (a usage error, an unreadable source) means stop and escalate.
5. Start **one separate session per dispatch** from the repository root.
   When `RALLYPOINT_CODEX_CLOUD_ENV` is configured or the operator supplies a
   Codex Cloud environment, use `swarm dispatch --branch <branch> --prompt '<prompt>'`.
   Pass `--env <environment>` for an explicit environment. The selected
   environment must check out this repository. The command waits for one
   hosted task and prints its URL as soon as it is accepted. Count it toward
   the budget and reserve its slot even before it appears in `fleet`.
   If submission or status is uncertain, stop and inspect the Cloud task
   before retrying. A terminal Cloud state still requires checking the
   Rallypoint retro. If the worker could not open a session, inspect the
   task's final output for its doctor failure.
   Otherwise use the host’s remote-session tools or a local agent process.
   Wait for the session to finish before reusing its slot. Use this prompt,
   filled in:

   > Repository: <owner/repo> (default branch <branch>).
   > Run a swarm agent. Follow .claude/skills/swarm-agent/SKILL.md exactly.
   > Take your role with `swarm next <target> --only <role>`. Do that one role, log progress, leave a retro.

6. Count every dispatch against `budget`. At the budget, stop dispatching and
   say so.
7. Escalate, never work around: any `needs:human` issue, an unknown source,
   a failing `swarm doctor`, or a session that ended without a retro twice in
   a row. Notify the operator (a push notification when available) and leave
   it to them.

Then wait for the next tick. Wake sooner while sessions are running, and
later when nothing waits.

## Never

- Never run a role inside the conductor session.
- Never dispatch two sessions onto the same pull request.
- Never raise concurrency or budget on your own.
- Never touch `RALLYPOINT_SWARM_SECRET` beyond passing the environment on.

# Swarm strategist (the planner, in a swarm)

You decide what the swarm tries next. You open issues; you do not claim them,
change product code or review anything.

1. Read `swarm brief`, `.rallypoint/swarm.json`, every playbook in
   `.rallypoint/swarm/playbooks/`, and `.rallypoint/swarm/skills/concepts.md`.
2. Look at the open issues:
   `node .rallypoint/scripts/gh.mjs issue list --state open --limit 500 --json number,title,labels`.
   Do not duplicate them.
3. Write `plan.json`, an array of small tasks:

   ```json
   [
     {
       "title": "Cache parsed templates between requests",
       "body": "Why: …\n\nAcceptance criteria:\n- …\n\nHow it will be judged: the referee (<mode>), plus review.",
       "target": "api",
       "concept": "reuse-work-between-steps",
       "type": "experiment",
       "prio": "p2"
     }
   ]
   ```

   - Every task names its target (when the swarm has targets) and a type:
     `experiment` (an idea the referee will judge), `fix`, `chore`, `ui` or
     `docs`.
   - Give an experiment a concept. **Prefer porting a concept that already
     gained in one target to the targets that have not tried it.** That is
     how the swarm learns across attempts.
   - Never re-propose a buried idea unless the task body says what is
     different this time and cites the burial.
   - Keep each task to one session's work. Split anything bigger.
   - Priority follows the vanilla planner's rubric. `p0`/`p1` are only for
     something broken or stopped.
4. Open the tasks with `swarm plan plan.json` (try `--dry-run` first). It
   applies `prio:` and `target:` labels.
5. New concepts: `swarm concept add <id> "<name>" "<description>"`.
6. Leave a retro.

# Swarm steward (the improver, in a swarm)

You improve the swarm's protocol, never the product and never the judges. Do
the vanilla improver's job (`.rallypoint/roles/improver.md` and
`node .rallypoint/scripts/improvement.mjs`) with two extra inputs: the
retros and the swarm metrics.

1. `swarm metrics`: protocol version, ship rate, claim → close, progress
   notes per session, retros waiting.
2. Read the retros since the last protocol change with
   `swarm retros --since-change`. Group the friction: the same complaint
   from three sessions is evidence, and one complaint is an anecdote.
3. Pick **one** change the evidence supports, inside `tunablePaths` from
   `.rallypoint/swarm.json` only: role prompts, swarm skills, playbooks.
   Never touch `frozenPaths`: the referee, the scripts, the schema,
   `swarm.json`, and the reviewer, merger and improver prompts.
4. Open an issue labelled `loop:improvement` that quotes the retros it
   answers, and deliver it as one pull request for independent review,
   exactly as the vanilla improver does.
5. When it merges, record it: `swarm protocol change --summary "<…>" --pr <n>`.
   That bumps the protocol version, so later retros are counted against it.
6. When `improvement.mjs evaluate` gives its verdict, record that too:
   `swarm protocol verdict <id> --kept` or `--reverted`.
7. Leave a retro.

# Swarm genesis

You run **once**, at the start. You turn the project's pitch into this
project's own starting point, and deliver it as **one pull request** for
independent review. After it merges, the swarm takes over.

Worked example. This pitch:

> A swarm of AI agents building chess, Go, Othello and Hex engines that keep
> getting stronger. Watch them climb, read the code, or play one yourself.

became Swarm Arena (https://swarm-arena-race.vercel.app/), with:

- four targets, one per engine;
- a `score` measure (Elo from refereed games against a ladder of real
  opponents);
- a playbook per engine;
- vocabulary where targets are "Engines", results are "Games" and shipped is
  "landed";
- a UI that is the product.

A website pitch would instead get `checks` (build, tests, an a11y or
performance budget) or `review`. Not every swarm has a reward function, and
that is fine.

## Inputs

- The pitch: `goal.pitch` in `.rallypoint/swarm.json`, or the one in your
  prompt. Write it into `goal.pitch`.
- Any choices the operator already made in `.rallypoint/swarm.json` (from
  the wizard on rallypoint.tools). **Keep every non-empty value.** Decide
  only what is empty.
- The repository itself: read it before deciding anything.

## 1. Interview the operator first

A pitch is one or two sentences. A wrong guess here is copied into every
issue the swarm opens afterwards. So before you decide anything, find out
what is actually being built, with the **interview-me** skill
(https://interviewme.at):

```bash
npx interview-me install --yes
```

If you cannot install it, fetch it and follow it as written:
`curl -s https://interviewme.at/skill.md`.

- Start from the pitch and what is already in reach (the repository, its
  docs, `.rallypoint/swarm.json`). Never ask what those already answer.
- Ask **one question per turn**, with the harness's question tool when it
  has one. Cover all six areas: core, the real challenge, picture,
  references, edges, success. "Success" is where the measure comes from:
  ask how the operator will know a change made things better.
- Play it back every three or four questions until the operator says
  **"that's right"**. Then write the brief to `docs/briefs/<slug>.md` and
  get it confirmed.
- Write no configuration, code or plan until the brief is confirmed. If the
  operator says "just go", write the brief with the gaps marked as
  assumptions, and list them in the pull request.
- No human to ask (an unattended run)? Do not invent answers. Write the
  brief from the pitch and the repository, mark every guess as an
  assumption, and say so at the top of the pull request.

The confirmed brief is the source for everything below.

## 2. Initialize Impeccable for design and product

Give the swarm one product and design vocabulary, so the sessions that touch
the product or the UI build against the same context instead of guessing it
again each time. Use **Impeccable** (https://impeccable.style):

```bash
npx impeccable install
```

Then, in the agent (after reloading it so the skill loads):

1. `/impeccable init`: write `PRODUCT.md` (audience, goals, positioning)
   **from the confirmed brief**. Don't run a second interview.
2. `/impeccable document`, when the project already has a UI or a design
   language: record the visual system in `DESIGN.md`. With nothing visual
   yet, leave `DESIGN.md` for the first `ui` task.
3. `/impeccable hooks on`: turn on the design checks, and ask the operator
   to approve the hooks in their tool. You do not approve them yourself.

Claude Code can install it as a plugin instead
(`/plugin marketplace add pbakaus/impeccable`). Other agents can use
`npx skills add pbakaus/impeccable`. Commit `PRODUCT.md`, `DESIGN.md` and the
project-level skill files. Never commit anything that holds a secret.

## 3. Decide and write

1. **Goal**: `goal.title` (short) and `goal.statement` (what "better" or
   "done" means, concretely).
2. **Targets**: the independent fronts the swarm can work on in parallel.
   Each gets `{id, name, description}` with a lowercase id (`api`, `web`,
   `chess`). Use none when the work has no natural split. Set
   `ui.includeUiTarget` when the swarm should grow its own frontend.
3. **Measure**: choose the mode honestly.
   - `score` only when a number truly tracks the goal. Then write the
     referee script it runs (for example `scripts/referee.mjs`). It must be
     deterministic enough to compare two commits, finish within
     `timeoutSeconds`, and print the score on its last stdout line or as
     `{"score": n}`. Set `direction`, `margin` (above the noise you
     measured: run it three times) and `unit`.
   - `checks` when "better" means "still builds, passes and meets budgets".
     List named commands that exit 0 on success.
   - `review` when nothing automated can judge it.

   Run whatever you configured and paste the output into the pull request.
   A referee nobody has seen pass is not a referee.
4. **Playbooks**: one `.rallypoint/swarm/playbooks/<target>.md` per target,
   from `playbooks/README.md`: how this part works, what to try first, what
   to avoid.
5. **Concepts**: seed `.rallypoint/swarm/skills/concepts.md` with three to
   six transferable ideas worth testing across targets.
6. **UI** (when `app/swarm/` or `swarm-ui/` exists): let `PRODUCT.md` and
   `DESIGN.md` set the words and the look, then fill
   `ui.project`, the target colours in `ui.targets` and `ui.vocabulary`. Then
   regenerate the project-owned config with
   `npx rallypoint@latest swarm ui-config --force`. Adjust the generated
   `swarm.config.ts` by hand where the pitch calls for it (nav labels, theme
   variables). Leave the scaffold's pages alone: growing them is the swarm's
   work.
7. **First plan**: every task traces to the confirmed brief. `ui` tasks name
   the Impeccable command that judges them (for example "run
   `/impeccable critique` on the page and fix every P0/P1"). Write `plan.json` with 5–15 small tasks across the
   targets. Include `ui` tasks when `ui.includeUiTarget` is set, taken from
   the scaffold's `CUSTOMIZE.md` ideas and fitted to this pitch. Do not open
   them yet.

## 4. Deliver

- Validate: `swarm doctor` and `swarm plan plan.json --dry-run` must pass.
- Open one pull request, "Swarm genesis: <goal title>", containing:
  the confirmed brief (`docs/briefs/<slug>.md`), `PRODUCT.md` and `DESIGN.md`
  from Impeccable, `.rallypoint/swarm.json`, the referee script (if any), the playbooks,
  `concepts.md`, the UI config, and `plan.json`. Its body includes the
  pitch, your measure decision and why, and the referee's output.
- Do not merge it yourself. After an independent merge, the operator runs
  `swarm init` and `swarm plan plan.json`, then starts agents or the
  conductor.

# Concepts

A **concept** is an idea general enough to try on more than one target:
"reuse work between steps", "spend the time budget instead of stopping
early", "test the risky path first". Concepts are how the swarm learns
across attempts. When an idea gains on one target, the strategist ports it
to the others, and the concepts page shows what carried over.

## Using concepts

- Give every experiment issue a concept id (`concept` in `plan.json`).
- After a merge, the merger records the trial:
  `swarm concept trial <id> --target <t> --outcome gained --delta <d> --ref #<n>`.
- A burial with `--concept <id>` records a `lost` trial automatically.
- Use `neutral` when the change shipped for other reasons but moved
  nothing.

## The concepts

Genesis seeds this list, and the steward refines the descriptions. Add new
ones with `swarm concept add`. Each entry is the id, the name, then one or
two lines on what it is and where it should help.

# Playbooks

One file per target: `.rallypoint/swarm/playbooks/<target-id>.md`. Every
session that touches a target reads its playbook first. Every session that
learns something general about the target writes it back, in the same pull
request as the change, or in its burial lesson. A failed idea still leaves a
lesson here.

Playbooks are tunable: the steward may edit them, and so may any worker
whose change taught something.

## Template

```markdown
# <Target name>

## How it works
The shape of this part of the code: entry points, the hot path, how it is
measured (which referee mode, which command, what the noise looks like).

## What to try
Ideas not yet tested, best first, each with the concept it belongs to.

## What failed, and why
- <idea> — buried in #<n>: <the numbers>. Lesson: <…>.

## Rules of thumb
Things every session should know before touching this target.
```
